profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal planning meeting for a new reanalysis stream within a TCGA Pan-Cancer project team at an academic cancer center. The team is preparing an integrated comparison across the original 12 TCGA tumor types, combining multi-omic matrices with clinical annotations to produce an overview deck and analysis plan for a cross-disease working group. The agenda is to agree on what data snapshot to use, what counts as the analysis cohort, how much clinical cleanup is needed before integration, who owns each workstream, and what should be delivered by the first review date. The expected outcome is a division of labor and timeline that appears aligned on cohort assembly, clinical harmonization, and a March 28 review package.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.expertise: Multi-omic integration, tumor clustering, TCGA matrix processing, reproducible analysis pipelines
members.background: A faculty-level computational biologist who has led several cross-cancer integrative analyses and typically works from harmonized public data releases and analysis-ready matrices.
members.private_state: She wants to get the analysis moving quickly with a technically clean cohort and avoid weeks of manual annotation work that could delay clustering and figure generation.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'Pan-Cancer freeze,' they mean the current harmonized GDC-based snapshot already mirrored into the institute's analysis environment.
A 'complete case' for this project means a tumor sample that has all required molecular layers present for integrative analysis, not merely partial data plus clinical fields.
Clinical 'harmonization' is mostly light standardization of a few columns such as disease code, age, sex, and survival endpoints because deeper curation was already done upstream.
If a deck is 'ready for review,' it only needs to be coherent enough for internal scientific discussion among core analysts, even if counts and annotations are not final.

members.name: David Morales
members.expertise: Clinical data integration, pathology/metadata coordination, consortium deliverables, oncology reporting workflows
members.background: A senior program manager who bridges bioinformatics, pathology, and disease leads, and who often builds cross-study clinical tables from legacy TCGA resources used in prior consortium presentations.
members.private_state: He wants the first deliverable to be presentation-safe for a broader steering group and is trying to prevent rework later by making sure clinical and cohort accounting are fully reconciled from the start.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention the 'Pan-Cancer freeze,' they mean the legacy Firehose-era snapshot tied to the subtype tables and pathology notes already used by the group.

A 'complete case' means a patient record that can be counted and interpreted clinically, even if some omics layers are missing, as long as core covariates and at least one molecular profile are present.

Clinical 'harmonization' includes resolving duplicated follow-up rows, stage-version inconsistencies, treatment-line fields, and disease-specific annotation quirks before the dataset is really usable.
If something is 'ready for review,' it should be stable enough to circulate outside the core analysis team without major caveats or changing sample counts.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to needing 'complete-case counts' for each tumor type.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means only tumors with all required molecular modalities available for integrative analysis, specifically expression, copy number, methylation, and RPPA in the joined analysis matrix.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means cases that are sufficiently documented for cohort summaries, with core clinical fields populated and at least one usable molecular profile.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is standard and sounds precise, so each assumes the other is using the conventional meaning from their own subcommunity; the meeting focuses on planning, not on sample-accounting definitions.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will work from 'the Pan-Cancer freeze' or 'the frozen set.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the institute's current GDC-harmonized hg38-aligned snapshot that feeds her reproducible multi-omic pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the older Firehose-era freeze because the group's subtype labels, pathology references, and prior reporting templates were built around it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both data snapshots are real, institutionally familiar, and routinely described as the Pan-Cancer freeze; because neither expects multiple plausible freezes to still be in use, the term feels unambiguous.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that David will 'harmonize the clinical sheet' before integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means a relatively narrow cleanup: aligning field names, standardizing endpoint columns, and ensuring disease codes match sample IDs used in the omics matrices.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes deeper reconciliation work such as resolving duplicate follow-up entries, recoding stage systems across tumor types, and normalizing treatment-history fields for broader reporting use.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The task label sounds like routine background work, so neither side feels a need to unpack its boundaries; both see it as a supporting step rather than a primary design decision.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They set a goal to have an 'overview deck ready for review' by March 28.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means an internal draft with the core pan-cancer plots, provisional cohort counts, and placeholder interpretation notes so the science leads can react.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a steering-committee-ready package with reconciled counts, disease-page notes, and enough annotation stability that it can be safely shared beyond the immediate analysis team.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same deadline language and both expect a slide deck, but their professional contexts set different quality thresholds; in a cooperative planning conversation, 'review' sounds naturally shared.
